To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
diagnostic ultrasound pulses with an MI of 1.0-2.5 that produce stable or inertial cavitation can restore skeletal muscle microvascular flow after acute arterial thrombosis.
high-mechanical index ultrasound impulses, which produce stable and inertial cavitation, restore skeletal microvascular blood flow in acute arterial thrombo-embolism.
diagnostic ultrasound impulses that produce inertial cavitation can restore microvascular flow after acute peripheral arterial thromboemboli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel ultrasound techniques for the non-invasive treatment of thromboembolic diseases.
the development of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of acute arterial thromboemobolism.
the development of new therapeutic ultrasound applications for the treatment of acute arterial thrombo-embolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high MI impulses can restore microvascular blood flow and this effect is not mediated by NO.

the intermittent high-MI pulses from a diagnostic ultrasound transducer can restore microvascular flow after arterial thromboembolic occlusion, and that this effect may not depend on the nitric oxide pathway.
high mechanical index ultrasound impulses can restore microvascular flow in the setting of acute arterial thrombo-embolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diagnostic ultrasound impulses with an MI that produces IC can restore microvascular flow in peripheral arterial thromboemboli.
the use of high mechanical index ultrasound impulses can restore microvascular flow and that this is not dependent on the nitric oxide system.
diagnostic transducer pulses can be used to restore skeletal muscle perfusion after acute thromboembolic obstruction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diagnostic ultrasound impulses can be used to restore microvascular blood flow in peripheral arterial thromboembolic disease.
high mechanical index impulses from a diagnostic ultrasound transducer can reverse acute arterial occlusion and improve microvascular blood volume.
diagnostic ultrasound with a high MI, but not a diagnostic ultrasound with a low MI, can be used to restore skeletal muscle blood flow after acute arterial embolism.
